bull_bear.body:
- Net cash INR 2,384 cr; net worth INR 9,464 cr — exceptional balance-sheet strength, deleveraged.
- Working-capital build-up mainly PSU receivables, anticipated and priced into tenders; largely serviced via non-fund-based limits; WC days could improve in secular growth.
- DevCo land capital ring-fenced ~INR 300 cr threshold. No dividend mention.
- DTA recognition boosts book PAT but is non-cash.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- DSM tightening (CERC plus/minus 15→10%; new projects on fossil-fuel deviation from 1-Apr-2026) — currently stayed but mgmt expects implementation; turbine performance/penalty risk, mitigated by forecasting service.
- Working-capital / PSU receivables stretch; OCF (~INR 12 bn) well below EBITDA (~INR 30 bn) for FY26.
- Order intake lumpy — Q4 intake "tad muted"; EPC deals take longer to close.
- INR depreciation / commodity (steel) — partly pass-through, residual exposure.
- Execution: 971-975 MW erected-but-not-commissioned (~350 MW awaiting customer last-mile).
- New CEO (Ajay Kapur) transition; APERC tariff approval pending for 775 MW FDRE; FDRE/solar-BESS strategy unproven for Suzlon.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- Confident, delivery-focused; J.P.C explicitly scored FY26 against prior commitments (60% growth promised → 63% EBITDA, 65% WTG rev) — high accountability.
- New CEO Ajay Kapur (ex-Ambuja Cements MD) signals professionalization; emphasis on leading vs lagging indicators, line-org rejuvenation.
- Resisted giving hard FY27 delivery guidance ("putting words in my mouth") — disciplined but slightly opaque; acknowledged investor request for monthly installation data, "will evaluate."
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Reported PAT inflated by INR 742 cr DTA (FY) / Q4 reported PAT INR 281 cr ex-adjustment — cash earnings materially lower than headline PAT.
- The strategic crux is the shift from product OEM to project developer (DevCo): margin/order-book lumpiness near-term but converts Suzlon into the sector's execution-bottleneck solver.
- Evening peak demand data (solar 0%, wind 21% contribution) is mgmt's core bull case for structural FDRE/wind bid revival.
- Europe re-entry interest is for legacy 2-3 MW series, not just new Blue Sky turbines — faster monetization optionality.
- Exceptional INR 70 cr is SE Forge arbitration win (in favour), NOT an OMS problem as analysts feared.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Full-stack, integrated wind-first model spanning technology (RE Tech), project development (RE DevCo), EPC execution (RE Projects) and long-term asset management (RE AMS), positioned as a single end-to-end renewable energy partner rather than a point-solution vendor
- Flagship S144 turbine certified as having the lowest product carbon footprint among wind turbines (6.17 gCO2/kWh across its lifecycle), independently verified by Indian Register Quality Systems (IRQS)
- Large installed O&M service base spanning 22,000+ MW as of July 31, 2026, supporting recurring service revenue and client stickiness
- Sustained R&D investment of Rs. 726.01 Crore in FY26 (up 106.12% year-on-year) directed at improving environmental and social impact of products
- PSU and C&I customer segments together account for 66% of the ~5.9 GW order book, indicating a diversified, less cyclical demand base
- S144 has garnered nearly 9,000 MW of cumulative orders to date, and WTG business grew at a 55% CAGR over the last three years
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Restatement of comparative FY25 financials pursuant to a court-approved Scheme of Arrangement — Statutory auditors flagged that comparative financial information for the year ended March 31, 2025 was restated in both standalone and consolidated financial statements to give effect to a Scheme of Arrangement (NCLT order dated April 29, 2026, effective from Appointed Date September 30, 2024), reducing straightforward historical comparability.
- Internal-controls / IT-systems transition gap during ERP migration — Statutory auditors noted the audit trail feature was not operative at the database level for an initial period (May 1-10, 2025 company-wide, and up to May 10, 2025 for a few domestic subsidiaries) during the Company's migration from SAP ECC to SAP S/4 HANA, a Ministry of Corporate Affairs compliance requirement; management stated no tampering was observed.
- Delays in statutory dues deposits — Statutory auditors observed a slight delay in a few cases in depositing certain statutory dues in the standalone financial statements; management attributed the delay to technical issues.
- Key managerial personnel transition / compliance timing gap — The Secretarial Auditor flagged that the Chief Financial Officer joined after the stipulated 3-month period under Regulation 26A of the Listing Regulations, following the prior Group CFO's resignation (effective August 31, 2025); the Board filled the vacancy within 3 months but the incoming CFO's actual joining exceeded that window.

outlook.body:
- Industry installations: ~8 GW FY27, ~10 GW FY28, ~15 GW by FY30/31 (Suzlon expects to track market +/-).
- Mgmt declined to give absolute FY27 delivery number; pointed to past trend (700→1,550→2,456 MW) and "positive trend to continue."
- EPC share of order book: 28% now → targeting 50% by FY28.
- WTG margins: "don't think materially can go down" in FY27; steel largely pass-through.
- EPC order closures from AP DevCo pipeline expected to start being announced "from June onwards."
- Capex run-rate ~INR 600 cr +/- 50 over next 3-4 years (vs ~INR 550 cr FY26).
- DTA: only deferred-tax CHARGE (non-cash) hits P&L next 2 years; ~INR 3,000-3,500 cr unrecognized DTA remaining.
outlook.title: Guidance (verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Order book 5.9 GW; 66% C&I + PSU. Post-quarter Sunsure order takes effective book to ~6 GW.
- S144 (3.X MW) cumulative order intake ~9 GW — flagship platform.
- DevCo identified-sites pipeline 22-23 GW; ~8 GW in active development (land acquisition / land contracts signed). "Slightly higher" now.
- AP PIA: 2.1 GW development rights, extended 24 months by new AP govt (Apr). 775 MW with PPA → being converted to FDRE (APERC tariff pending); balance 1,325 MW → firm EPC contracts to be monetized over next 6 months from June.
- NTPC moving from split contracts (BOP + WTG) to turnkey EPC: 215 MW in AP already, plus expected 540 MW + 2,000 MW in AP. Mgmt sees Suzlon strong in PSU EPC.
- ArcelorMittal EPC order came out of the DevCo pipeline.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- DevCo / land-bank development model — convert dynamic 22-23 GW identified sites into EPC contracts; "engine for growth of the sector," unlocks execution bottleneck.
- FDRE / hybrid (wind + solar + BESS) — intent to supply full RE stack; solar/BESS "very much on agenda" but no acquisition imminent; strategy (asset-light vs invest) TBD.
- Scheduling & forecasting service — monetizing DSM tightening (plus/minus 15% → 10%) as add-on service; collaborating with international players.
- European/export re-entry via Blue Sky; repowering opportunity (India fleet 56 GW installed, FY26 installs highest since 2017).
- RE parks with transferable GNA connectivity — working with GoI on regulation change.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Global wind industry outlook remains strong: GWEC projects annual global installations reaching 178 GW in 2026 and averaging ~194 GW per year between 2026-2030 (CAGR 5.2%), a large and growing addressable market for wind OEMs like Suzlon
- Post-geopolitical energy disruptions, countries are prioritising energy security and diversifying away from fossil fuels, positioning wind as a domestic, scalable, cost-competitive power source and a structural demand driver
- As renewable penetration rises, focus is shifting from pure capacity growth to system integration, flexibility and reliability, driving demand for hybrid and storage-integrated (firm and dispatchable renewable energy / FDRE) configurations combining wind, solar and storage
- India's economy remains resilient with GDP growth projected at 6.4% (2026) and 6.7% (2027) per IMF, supporting continued electricity demand growth and the domestic renewable energy build-out
- Asia-Pacific, led by China and India, remains the largest and fastest-growing wind market, accounting for nearly 80% of global installations in 2025; India was among the top 5 markets for new wind installations (6.4 GW in 2025)

guidance (verify next quarter):

order book & pipeline:
- Order book 5.9 GW; 66% C&I + PSU. Post-quarter Sunsure order takes effective book to ~6 GW.
- S144 (3.X MW) cumulative order intake ~9 GW — flagship platform.
- DevCo identified-sites pipeline 22-23 GW; ~8 GW in active development (land acquisition / land contracts signed). "Slightly higher" now.
- AP PIA: 2.1 GW development rights, extended 24 months by new AP govt (Apr). 775 MW with PPA → being converted to FDRE (APERC tariff pending); balance 1,325 MW → firm EPC contracts to be monetized over next 6 months from June.
- NTPC moving from split contracts (BOP + WTG) to turnkey EPC: 215 MW in AP already, plus expected 540 MW + 2,000 MW in AP. Mgmt sees Suzlon strong in PSU EPC.
- ArcelorMittal EPC order came out of the DevCo pipeline.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **WTG**: rev INR 14,040 cr FY (+65%), contribution margin 24.5%. 4.5 GW manufacturing capacity fully operational; adding 3 AI-enabled smart blade factories.
- **OMS (Renom)**: 15.7+ GW under management India, machine availability >95%; AUM growing on fleet additions. Q2 EBITDA dip recouped — full-year OMS EBITDA 40.5% (was flagged one-off).
- **SE Forge**: rev INR 597 cr (+22%), EBITDA INR 119 cr (+61%), domestic + export driven; INR 70 cr exceptional arbitration gain.
- **EPC / DevCo**: new growth engine; land-to-commissioning turnkey; full FDRE (RE) stack intent vs just wind portion.
- **Exports / Blue Sky**: re-entry into Europe via Spain launch (S175, S163 turbines); strong developer/IPP/utility interest also for legacy 2 MW & 3 MW series; mgmt sees future big revenue + bottom-line driver.
growth verticals / optionality:
- DevCo / land-bank development model — convert dynamic 22-23 GW identified sites into EPC contracts; "engine for growth of the sector," unlocks execution bottleneck.
- FDRE / hybrid (wind + solar + BESS) — intent to supply full RE stack; solar/BESS "very much on agenda" but no acquisition imminent; strategy (asset-light vs invest) TBD.
- Scheduling & forecasting service — monetizing DSM tightening (plus/minus 15% → 10%) as add-on service; collaborating with international players.
- European/export re-entry via Blue Sky; repowering opportunity (India fleet 56 GW installed, FY26 installs highest since 2017).
- RE parks with transferable GNA connectivity — working with GoI on regulation change.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Consol EBITDA margin 18.1% (+100 bps YoY); WTG contribution margin 24.5%.
- Steel largely pass-through (except some PSU contracts); FX partly pass-through; cost-management drives mitigate INR depreciation impact.
- Levers: S144 scale (9 GW) enabling supplier renegotiation; supply diversification + Make-in-India; R&D-led value engineering; annual cost-cut target.
- Mgmt: WTG margins shouldn't materially fall FY27; unsure how much pricing can be raised — relies on business-model reorientation (EPC + DevCo).
capex / expansion:
- FY26 capex ~INR 550 cr; future run-rate ~INR 600 cr +/- 50 over 3-4 yrs.
- Manufacturing 4.5 GW operational; adding 3 AI-enabled smart blade factories.
- DevCo working capital deployed ~INR 300-350 cr (threshold framework); more WC / non-fund-based facility needed as model scales and connectivity added.
capital allocation:
- Net cash INR 2,384 cr; net worth INR 9,464 cr — exceptional balance-sheet strength, deleveraged.
- Working-capital build-up mainly PSU receivables, anticipated and priced into tenders; largely serviced via non-fund-based limits; WC days could improve in secular growth.
- DevCo land capital ring-fenced ~INR 300 cr threshold. No dividend mention.
- DTA recognition boosts book PAT but is non-cash.
risks & watch-items:
- DSM tightening (CERC plus/minus 15→10%; new projects on fossil-fuel deviation from 1-Apr-2026) — currently stayed but mgmt expects implementation; turbine performance/penalty risk, mitigated by forecasting service.
- Working-capital / PSU receivables stretch; OCF (~INR 12 bn) well below EBITDA (~INR 30 bn) for FY26.
- Order intake lumpy — Q4 intake "tad muted"; EPC deals take longer to close.
- INR depreciation / commodity (steel) — partly pass-through, residual exposure.
- Execution: 971-975 MW erected-but-not-commissioned (~350 MW awaiting customer last-mile).
- New CEO (Ajay Kapur) transition; APERC tariff approval pending for 775 MW FDRE; FDRE/solar-BESS strategy unproven for Suzlon.
management quality / tone:
- Confident, delivery-focused; J.P.C explicitly scored FY26 against prior commitments (60% growth promised → 63% EBITDA, 65% WTG rev) — high accountability.
- New CEO Ajay Kapur (ex-Ambuja Cements MD) signals professionalization; emphasis on leading vs lagging indicators, line-org rejuvenation.
- Resisted giving hard FY27 delivery guidance ("putting words in my mouth") — disciplined but slightly opaque; acknowledged investor request for monthly installation data, "will evaluate."
non-obvious takeaways:
- Reported PAT inflated by INR 742 cr DTA (FY) / Q4 reported PAT INR 281 cr ex-adjustment — cash earnings materially lower than headline PAT.
- The strategic crux is the shift from product OEM to project developer (DevCo): margin/order-book lumpiness near-term but converts Suzlon into the sector's execution-bottleneck solver.
- Evening peak demand data (solar 0%, wind 21% contribution) is mgmt's core bull case for structural FDRE/wind bid revival.
- Europe re-entry interest is for legacy 2-3 MW series, not just new Blue Sky turbines — faster monetization optionality.
- Exceptional INR 70 cr is SE Forge arbitration win (in favour), NOT an OMS problem as analysts feared.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Suzlon Energy is a leading Indian renewable energy solutions provider that designs and manufactures wind turbine generators (flagship model S144) and increasingly solar and storage technology, and executes end-to-end EPC/project delivery for utility-scale renewable projects. It also provides long-term operations, maintenance and asset management services to a large installed fleet of wind assets, serving primarily PSU (public sector) and C&I (commercial & industrial) customers in India.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Full-stack, integrated wind-first model spanning technology (RE Tech), project development (RE DevCo), EPC execution (RE Projects) and long-term asset management (RE AMS), positioned as a single end-to-end renewable energy partner rather than a point-solution vendor
- Flagship S144 turbine certified as having the lowest product carbon footprint among wind turbines (6.17 gCO2/kWh across its lifecycle), independently verified by Indian Register Quality Systems (IRQS)
- Large installed O&M service base spanning 22,000+ MW as of July 31, 2026, supporting recurring service revenue and client stickiness
- Sustained R&D investment of Rs. 726.01 Crore in FY26 (up 106.12% year-on-year) directed at improving environmental and social impact of products
- PSU and C&I customer segments together account for 66% of the ~5.9 GW order book, indicating a diversified, less cyclical demand base
- S144 has garnered nearly 9,000 MW of cumulative orders to date, and WTG business grew at a 55% CAGR over the last three years

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- DSM tightening (CERC plus/minus 15→10%; new projects on fossil-fuel deviation from 1-Apr-2026) — currently stayed but mgmt expects implementation; turbine performance/penalty risk, mitigated by forecasting service.
- Working-capital / PSU receivables stretch; OCF (~INR 12 bn) well below EBITDA (~INR 30 bn) for FY26.
- Order intake lumpy — Q4 intake "tad muted"; EPC deals take longer to close.
- INR depreciation / commodity (steel) — partly pass-through, residual exposure.
- Execution: 971-975 MW erected-but-not-commissioned (~350 MW awaiting customer last-mile).
- New CEO (Ajay Kapur) transition; APERC tariff approval pending for 775 MW FDRE; FDRE/solar-BESS strategy unproven for Suzlon.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- Reported PAT inflated by INR 742 cr DTA (FY) / Q4 reported PAT INR 281 cr ex-adjustment — cash earnings materially lower than headline PAT.
- The strategic crux is the shift from product OEM to project developer (DevCo): margin/order-book lumpiness near-term but converts Suzlon into the sector's execution-bottleneck solver.
- Evening peak demand data (solar 0%, wind 21% contribution) is mgmt's core bull case for structural FDRE/wind bid revival.
- Europe re-entry interest is for legacy 2-3 MW series, not just new Blue Sky turbines — faster monetization optionality.
- Exceptional INR 70 cr is SE Forge arbitration win (in favour), NOT an OMS problem as analysts feared.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
